context: Powerhouse continuity was already documented conceptually, but chats and agents were not yet explicitly enforced as intrinsic execution nodes inside one canonical Powerhouse loop with mandatory canonical-state preflight and canonical writeback before terminal completion.
problem: A chat or agent could otherwise be treated as a temporary helper around the system instead of a governed execution node inside it, creating risk of local-only state, repeated rediscovery, parallel truth, incomplete handoff and terminal success without reusable learning.
root_cause: The existing continuity authority required current-state-first and reuse-first behavior, but lacked an explicit machine-readable loop_node_contract and governed regression coverage proving that both chat and agent actors are intrinsic nodes of one canonical loop.

regression.coverage_rule: The regression is intentionally embedded in an already mandatory backend contract suite rather than a one-off test workflow.

incident_learning.symptom: Initial Required admission failed before expensive CI.
incident_learning.cause: The PR lacked the canonical delivery metadata required by the existing hygiene/admission gate.
incident_learning.fix: Added Obligation-ID, Delivery-Lane, Candidate-Type, Base-SHA and Supersedes metadata to the same PR lineage.
incident_learning.prevention: Every executable Powerhouse PR must carry canonical delivery metadata before expecting governed CI admission; do not weaken or bypass admission.

incident_learning.symptom: A newly added standalone regression test would not have run in the backend lane.
incident_learning.cause: The backend lane executes an explicit governed test set and the standalone file was outside that set.
incident_learning.fix: Moved the regression into tests/brain-powerhouse-universal-agent-learning-writeback.test.mjs, which is already part of the mandatory backend suite, then removed the standalone test file.
incident_learning.prevention: A regression only counts as protection when a required governed CI path actually executes it. Prefer existing governed test families over creating parallel test workflows.

incident_learning.symptom: Canonical Powerhouse continuity existed in policy, tests and documentation but was not yet exposed as a cross-runtime discoverable agent skill.
incident_learning.cause: The repository had no .agents/skills Powerhouse continuity entrypoint, so skill discovery could depend on reading AGENTS.md or canonical policy directly.
incident_learning.fix: Added .agents/skills/powerhouse-continuity/SKILL.md, linked it from AGENTS.md and continuity authority, and extended the governed universal learning/writeback regression to require the skill and its canonical references.
incident_learning.prevention: Material Powerhouse operating rules that require judgment across chats/agents must have one discoverable cross-runtime skill entrypoint backed by canonical policy and required CI; the skill never becomes a competing authority.

prevention: Treat every material chat and agent as an intrinsic execution node in the single canonical Powerhouse loop.
Never allow local chat state or local agent state to become an alternative source of truth.
Require canonical-state preflight before material execution.
Require canonical writeback of verified state, evidence, outcome, learning, prevention and remaining obligations before terminal completion.
Require the next capable chat or agent to resume from the updated canonical state rather than reconstructing prior work.
Do not claim a governance rule is protected unless a required CI lane executes its regression.
Do not bypass admission failures; repair the canonical candidate metadata or exact root cause on the same delivery lineage.
Keep the Powerhouse continuity skill as a discoverability layer over canonical policy; never fork policy truth into the skill.
